A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same BudgetMem research work, with 37 readable pages including Appendices A–C. Full text and rendered-page comparison identifies differences only in first-page dates/version labeling and two Table 1 values.

before.justification: v1 reports original BudgetMem evaluations on LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and HotpotQA in Tables 1 and 5–10, alongside reward-alignment ablation and retrieval-sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, and sensitivity analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The modular memory pipeline, shared router, three tiering strategies, cost-aware reward, and PPO procedure remain unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and HotpotQA tasks, including identical category coverage in Appendix B.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain ReadAgent, MemoryBank, A-MEM, LangMem, Mem0, MemoryOS, and LightMem. The A-MEM numerical revisions do not change comparator membership or implementation.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain the same splits, chunk sizes, top-K retrieval, F1/Judge/cost metrics, model configurations, transfer evaluation, and training budgets.

E4.justification: The reward-scale alignment ablation, budget-tier selection analysis, retrieval-size sensitivity study, and appendix category analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting, without stated repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: In Table 1's LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct A-MEM row, HotpotQA cost changes from 13.32 to 26.74 and average cost from 36.55 to 32.07. Appendix Table 9 reports 26.74 in both versions. All other results are unchanged; the revised average does not equal the mean of the revised dataset costs.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, pipeline equations, cost normalization, reward alignment, and PPO formulation in Equations 1–13 remain identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about query-aware budget routing, the three tiering strategies, and performance–cost trade-offs.

C2.justification: Interpretations of runtime cost efficiency, tiering behavior, reward alignment, and retrieval noise remain unchanged, as do applicability qualifications and the Impact Statement.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, model identifiers, preprocessing instructions, Appendix C prompts, and the code-access link are unchanged. No explanation of the revised cost entries is added.

R1.justification: Section 2, cited works, and the reference list are identical. The positioning relative to existing memory systems and inference-time cost-control research is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page preprint date changes from February 6 to May 21, 2026, and the arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated February 5 to v2 dated May 20. Prose, terminology, authors, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–10 retain identical designs, captions, positions, and surrounding layout. Table 1 changes only numerical cell contents, assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: v2 reconciles A-MEM's HotpotQA cost in Table 1 with Appendix Table 9, but changes its average from 36.55 to 32.07. The unchanged appendix costs—and now Table 1's costs—are 2.88, 80.02, and 26.74, averaging 36.55. Thus one discrepancy is repaired while an appendix-supported aggregate becomes incorrect. With the remaining scientific content unchanged, these opposing reporting effects leave the net quality direction unclear.
